hx_fit_circle_contour — 2D halcon_ext op

• Data kinds: contour → feature

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "hx_fit_circle_contour", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: fit_circle_contour_xld (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Stages (the ops that come before → this op, left to right):

▸ hx_fit_circle_contour: stages (docs site)

Usage

Fit a circle to the contour points by the algebraic (Kåsa) method and return the fit residual (RMS) — small = close to a circle.

Pools the points of all contours, fits a circle with Kåsa's algebraic method (solve [x, y, 1]·sol = x^2 + y^2 by least squares; centre (sol0/2, sol1/2), radius sqrt(sol2 + cx^2 + cy^2)), and returns the RMS of the difference between each point's distance from the centre and the radius, divided by max(H, W) and capped at 1, as np.float64. The circle parameters themselves are not returned.

• a, b are unused.

• 0.0 if there are fewer than 3 points (indistinguishable from a perfect circle). If the value under the radius square root is negative, the radius is treated as 0.

The algebraic method does not minimise geometric distance, so the radius is biased for short arcs (narrow angular range) and for outliers. For nearly collinear points the minimum-norm solution gives a very large radius and a small residual (a line looks like "a large circle"). To judge circularity, combine with hx_regress_contours to exclude lines. The radius of the enclosing circle is hx_smallest_circle_xld.

Try it in Studio

The program below has been verified to run (same input as the figure). In Studio's help this block becomes buttons that load and run it on the spot.

threshold 0.50 0.50
sk_find_contours 0.50 0.50
hx_fit_circle_contour 0.50 0.50
